introduction.en: The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) is a specialized agency of the United Nations that leads international efforts to defeat hunger. Established in 1945, it serves as a neutral forum where nations meet to negotiate agreements and debate policy.
introduction.hi: The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) is a specialized agency of the United Nations that leads international efforts to defeat hunger. Established in 1945, it serves as a neutral forum where nations meet to negotiate agreements and debate policy.

body.en: FAO contributes to global food security through normative work, such as setting food safety standards (Codex Alimentarius), and operational work, including capacity building for climate-resilient agriculture. For India, FAO provides critical data, technical expertise for sustainable farming, and support for initiatives like the International Year of Millets, which helps in diversifying India's food basket and improving nutritional outcomes.

conclusion.en: As India aims to transform its agricultural sector, the FAO's role in knowledge sharing and policy guidance remains vital for achieving sustainable development and food security.
